extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers and editors involved with EMBO Press life-science journals (submitters and peer-review participants)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and publication standards for submitting, reviewing, and publishing life-science manuscripts at EMBO Press journals, covering authorship, peer review, data and materials sharing, integrity, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship eligibility (ICMJE-derived criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every author must meet ALL of the following criteria: substantial contributions to conception/design or acquisition/analysis/interpretation of data; drafting or critical revision for important intellectual content; final approval of the version to be published; agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work in ensuring that accuracy/integrity questions are investigated and resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapted from ICMJE authorship guidelines. Authorship implies originality, accurate attribution of literature, and reproducibility. Violations may constitute scientific misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding authors must ensure all listed authors have received and approved the manuscript before submission; relay substantive correspondence and reviewer reports to all listed authors; verify that new data/materials/code comply with transparency and reproducibility standards; agree to make all data underlying figures available as source data linked to the paper; confirm presentation accurately reflects original sources; conform to journal sharing policies; and provide an institutional email address at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding authors carry responsibility for preservation and retrievability of original data/materials/code and for ensuring co-authors are informed. All authors are notified at first submission and at acceptance; other communication is to the designated corresponding author only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributor roles (CRediT) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of every author’s contribution must be specified using the Contributor Roles Taxonomy (CRediT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mandatory author contribution section must be included in every paper; free-text additional contributions may complement CRediT entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI cannot be listed as an author
rubrics_metrics.description: An Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Large Language Model (LLM) program cannot be listed as an author of an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must adhere to the journal’s AI tools policy (see related guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and disclosure of AI tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of AI programs should be primarily restricted to improve style, accessibility or quality of human-generated text and images. Any part of an article assembled with AI must be thoroughly checked and verified by authors, and authors bear full responsibility for factual accuracy and provenance of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose AI use in the published article, detailing which parts were assembled with AI and which tools were employed. AI may be used in collection/analysis of data if documented in Methods. Synthetic data generated by AI must be clearly labeled in main text and figures and documented in Methods. AI must not synthesize or edit experimental data in ways that misrepresent findings. AI-generated illustrative content is allowed if declared and attributed where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint posting and declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press journals encourage posting primary research manuscripts on recognised preprint servers before or in parallel with submission. Authors should declare preprint versions in the cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints (e.g., bioRxiv, medRxiv) will not be considered in evaluation of conceptual advance. Scooping protection applies from day of posting if manuscript submitted within 4 months. bioRxiv/medRxiv preprints auto-forward link to EMBO Press papers. Use recommended citation format for preprints. Policy applies to primary research but not to reviews/commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewed preprints and Review Commons affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press supports 'reviewed preprints' (preprints with public reviewer reports and author response) and affiliates with Review Commons to accept peer-reviewed manuscripts based on existing reviewer reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can request that reviewer reports acquired by EMBO Press journals be posted on the preprint. Review Commons affiliate manuscripts are assessed based on existing reports; affiliates consider the same reviewer reports to avoid serial submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scooping protection (standard and extended)
rubrics_metrics.description: During editorial and peer review and the agreed author revision period, other studies that appear are not taken into account in assessing conceptual advance. Scooping protection applies from the day of posting a manuscript on a recognised preprint server, provided submission to the journal occurs within 4 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should inform editors when they become aware of other studies directly relevant to their study. Manuscripts with overlapping authors are not subject to scooping protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and options
rubrics_metrics.description: Default single-anonymous peer review (reviewers know authors; reports anonymous to authors). Authors may opt for double-anonymous review at initial submission (authors must anonymise manuscript).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors choose double-anonymous, they are responsible for anonymisation; editorial offices will not edit files to anonymise them and will not notify authors who failed to anonymise. The journal may consult reviewers on a de-anonymised manuscript after conditional acceptance to assess revision changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial triage and reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts undergo technical checks and assessment by a scientific editor (and possibly Editorial Advisory Board member or external expert). Research manuscripts judged potentially suitable with realistic experimental revision are sent for formal peer review, typically to three independent experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts with low probability of success may be returned without delay. Authors may exclude a small number of reviewers for potential conflicts; see EMBO Press reviewer guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision invitation and decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on reviewers' arguments/recommendations, editors decide to offer publication, request revision, or reject. Revisions are invited only for manuscripts that have a high probability of acceptance after one major round of experimental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions may involve consultation with reviewers, editorial board and/or authors. Authors can appeal editorial decisions or transfer manuscripts and reviewer identities through transfer systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymous review operational constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may choose double-anonymous review at submission but must anonymise their manuscript; editorial offices will not edit manuscript files for anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If anonymisation is incomplete, the office will not alert authors. Editors may consult reviewers after conditional acceptance on a de-anonymised manuscript to evaluate revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer cross-commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are routinely invited to comment on each other’s reports and may discuss issues under moderation of the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are not informed of each other’s identities. Cross-commenting is moderated by editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent review process and Review Process File
rubrics_metrics.description: For all accepted manuscripts EMBO Press publishes an online supplementary Review Process File containing all correspondence between authors and editorial office relevant to the decision (all reviewer comments directed to authors and authors’ point-by-point responses). Internal communications and informal consultations are excluded. Reviewer anonymity is strictly maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can opt out of the transparent process at any stage prior to publication; the author checklist will still be published even if authors opt out. The journal has removed the 'Confidential Comments' field so authors receive all information pertinent to the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: No confidential comments to authors in reviewer forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Confidential Comments' field has been removed; reviewers should be aware that all comments will be transmitted to authors and other reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers need to convey confidential concerns (ethical standards, data integrity, biosecurity, or conflicts) they should contact the editorial office by email rather than using confidential fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal experiment reporting and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: For studies reporting experiments on live vertebrates and/or higher invertebrates, the corresponding author must confirm experiments were performed in accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations and must include a statement in Materials and Methods identifying the institutional/licensing committee approving the experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors reserve the right to consult board members or external experts and to reject manuscripts that do not conform to NIH or MRC animal welfare guidelines. Authors are encouraged to follow ARRIVE guidelines for reporting animal studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects research ethics and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: For experiments involving human subjects, corresponding authors must identify the approving committee and include a statement that informed consent was obtained and that experiments conformed to the WMA Declaration of Helsinki and the Belmont Report principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors or reviewers may request further documentation. Any restrictions on availability or use of human data/samples should be clearly specified and may affect editorial decisions. Clinical trials require a CONSORT flow diagram (supplementary) and trial registration; retrospective registration is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow EQUATOR Network reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to follow appropriate EQUATOR Network reporting guidelines depending on study type (e.g., ARRIVE for animal research; CONSORT for parallel-group randomized trials; CARE, REMARK, STARD, MOOSE, PRISMA, STROBE, STREGA, STAMPL, MIAME, BRISQ for listed study types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific study-type guidance is listed and authors should consult EQUATOR and the cited guideline for reporting details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosecurity and dual-use assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned research and results should be evaluated early for possible dual-use concerns; authors should consult an appropriate local body regarding biosecurity/public health implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must describe any potential biosecurity implications and the local body's assessment in the cover letter and author checklist. Editors may balance risks/benefits and consult external experts; final publication decisions rest with editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity investigations and image screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal staff undertake routine image analysis of submitted manuscripts and may request source data and author responses to image aberrations. The journal will investigate suspected fraud, inappropriate image manipulation, plagiarism, misrepresentation, duplicate publication and other ethical violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations may lead to corrections, editorial expressions of concern, or retractions; authors’ employers and institutions may be informed. The journal will collaborate with independent institutional investigations and may accept their outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and prohibition of plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is misappropriation of intellectual property and substantial unattributed textual copying of another's work, including ideas, text, images or materials and methods. Any information published should represent a substantial, novel contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal reserves the right not to publish material already published in peer-reviewed journals or persistent media (preprints, conference materials, theses are exempt). Related manuscripts must be declared in the cover letter and included with submission. All material must be attributed per Associated Press standards. CrossCheck is used to screen for plagiarism/self-plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integrity of images — three-tiered classification and source data
rubrics_metrics.description: When potential aberrations in image-based data are noted, severity is classified according to a three-tiered system; authors will be contacted and, depending on severity, authors’ institutions may be contacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal staff analyze image-based data before acceptance; editors may request source data for any figure and may decline publication if key data fail data integrity, ethical or reproducibility standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and reagents sharing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: By publishing in EMBO Press, authors agree to make available to academic colleagues all new reagents (organisms, viruses, cells, nucleic acids, antibodies, etc.) used in the research that are not available from public repositories or commercial suppliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials should be made available at reasonable cost reflecting production/distribution. Distribution does not confer co-authorship. If third parties generated/analysed parts of the data, this must be stated in the data availability statement. Restrictions on availability should be clearly stated and may affect editorial decisions. Authors are encouraged to deposit plasmids to repositories such as Addgene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing and software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets obtained by experimentation, computation or data mining should be made freely available without restriction, especially data central to the paper's findings. Software should be described sufficiently to allow reproduction of algorithms and, if central, non-commercial users should be granted free access to implementations where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If software implementation is central, provide import/export functionalities for integration. Any restrictions on availability/use must be specified and may detract from impact and editorial decision. EMBO Press will only review/publish manuscripts if authors agree to make data that cannot be published in the journal itself available in appropriate public databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale datasets, sequences, atomic coordinates and computational models should be deposited in relevant public databases prior to submission, with private access available for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide username and password details in the manuscript file to enable reviewer access. Follow EMBO Press Data deposition guidance and recommended repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets and computer code generated in the study must be listed in a structured 'Data Availability' section after Methods. Each dataset should list: a short description of the measurement type, repository name, DOI/accession number, and a resolvable link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An example format is provided. If no datasets are included, authors should insert: 'This study includes no data deposited in external repositories'. See Source Data Submission Guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished observations and 'data not shown' policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal does not permit citation of 'Data not shown'. 'Unpublished observations' are allowed only in exceptional cases if peripheral to the major message and intended for future study; names of persons reporting such observations should be listed in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal communications must be authorised in writing and sent to the editorial office at submission. References to manuscripts in preparation should be cited as '(Author name(s), in preparation)' and copies should be enclosed at submission if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interest disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, reviewers, advisors, and editors are required to declare all potential or actual interests that could be perceived to influence presentation, interpretation, or assessment of an article at the earliest opportunity and before viewing/downloading relevant files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, potential reviewers/advisors/board members should discuss with the editor before agreeing to evaluate. Editors will exclude themselves from handling manuscripts owing to competing interests. Authors must include a declaration in the paper's disclosure statement; a full competing interest policy with example statements is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may appeal decisions if there is concrete evidence of a misunderstanding or mistake at the editorial or reviewer level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals should be sent by email to the handling editor; they are evaluated in depth and without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer policy (within EMBO Press and from other journals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may transfer manuscripts between EMBO Press journals or transfer submissions (with reviewer comments) from other journals; editors may confidentially consult with other EMBO Press journals or offer transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declined manuscripts include a link to transfer to other EMBO Press journals. Transfers may forward reviewer reports and identities (if reviewers agreed). Transfers from select Nature Portfolio journals to EMBO Press are possible via consultation. New submissions with reviewer comments from other journals are welcomed if accompanied by a cover letter, complete reviewer reports and a point-by-point response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article corrections, errata, editorial notes and addenda
rubrics_metrics.description: All reported issues will be assessed; corrections and additions are published at editors' discretion and only in exceptional cases. Definitions: correction (author error), erratum (journal error), editorial note (alert readers to specific issue), addendum (rare; additional data relevant to central aspects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For papers ten years or older, clear evidence of a data integrity issue affecting core claims is required to pursue action. Image integrity issues must meet Level 2/3 definitions. Authors must carefully review proofs; changes before issue assignment may be made with a footnote. Figure corrections trigger review of all figures and may require source data. Refutations/correspondence are peer reviewed at editor discretion; after one round of correspondence the matter is closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author name changes after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who have formally changed their name may request updates to their published paper; the journal will update the paper and metadata but will not publish a correction notice or retain documentation of the previous name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated metadata will be redelivered to indexing services (PubMed, PMC, Google Scholar). Citations to the paper will retain previous name. The author may choose a silent correction (no public note) or a formal Author Correction. Authors are requested to inform co-authors to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Content of papers and any associated press releases is strictly embargoed until the official publication date. Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media from one week before publication provided the journalist respects the embargo date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may arrange their own publicity but must adhere to embargo conditions. EMBO Press will press release selected papers with summaries; further details available from the editorial office.
